criteria.name: premise_urgency
criteria.description: The premise establishes concrete stakes and a reason things must happen NOW. Not a situation that could sit unresolved indefinitely. Test: if the premise could be summarized as 'two people exist near each other' with no pressure forcing action, score 0–35. If there is a ticking clock, an inciting event, or a threshold that has just been crossed, score 60+.

criteria.name: character_necessity
criteria.description: Each character is narratively load-bearing. Their secret creates potential conflict with at least one other character. Removing any one character would break something in the story. Test: if two characters could be merged without losing anything, score 0–40. If each character's presence creates a distinct pressure that wouldn't exist otherwise, score 70+.

criteria.name: world_constraint
criteria.description: The setting has rules or properties that actively constrain what characters can do — not just flavor text. The atmosphere and physical description are specific enough to generate consistent images. Test: if the setting is generic enough to work as the backdrop for any story in the genre, score 0–35. If the world's specific rules create at least one story problem that wouldn't exist in a different setting, score 65+.

criteria.name: thematic_focus
criteria.description: Themes are phrased as genuine questions with no obvious answer. They connect to the premise and the characters' secrets — not imported from outside. Test: if themes are abstract moral statements ('Power corrupts') with no connection to the specific characters, score 0–40. If themes are questions that the premise and character conflicts could plausibly explore, score 65+.

criteria.name: downstream_utility
criteria.description: All fields are populated with specific, usable content. speech_patterns are concrete enough that a writer could imitate them. appearance descriptions are specific enough for image generation. No placeholder or lorem ipsum content.
